instructions: Cut the chicken breast in half through the thickness to make 2 thinner pieces from each breast. Pat them dry and sprinkle both sides with the salt and half the pepper.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat for 1 minute. Add the chicken and cook for 4 minutes, until the underside is golden and lets go of the pan.

Flip it and cook the other side for 3 minutes. You're cooking it to 160°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Cut into the thickest piece: it's done when there's no pink left.
Transfer the chicken to a cutting board and let it rest for 5 minutes. Meanwhile, chop 4 cups of the romaine and lightly crush the croutons into 1/4 cup.
Slice the chicken into thin strips. In a bowl, toss the chicken with the Caesar dressing, the Parmesan and the remaining pepper.
Lay a tortilla flat and put a quarter of the romaine along the center. Add a quarter of the chicken and a quarter of the croutons.
Fold in the sides, then roll it up tightly from the bottom. Repeat with the rest of the tortillas and cut each in half.
Wrap each one tightly in foil or plastic wrap. They keep in the fridge for 2 days. The cooked chicken on its own keeps 3 days, so you can also assemble the wraps fresh each morning.
method_notes: No version of the dish we read had 20 or more ratings, so this is a fallback and leads with Jersey Girl Cooks (no rating shown): chicken tossed with Caesar dressing and Parmesan, rolled with romaine, croutons and tortilla. Six Sisters' Stuff (5 from 1 vote) is a different build with a cream cheese spread, olives and cheddar, so this skips it. This one cooks and slices its own chicken breast instead of using already cooked chicken, and drops the cucumber. Jersey Girl Cooks gives 2 days for assembled wraps and up to 4 days for the chicken.
